what: Smithfield Foods is America's largest pork producer: it raises hogs, slaughters and processes them, and sells fresh pork and packaged meats under Smithfield, Eckrich and Nathan's Famous.
customers: Supermarkets, food service distributors and export markets, especially in Asia and Mexico.
money: bacon, sausage, ham and hot dogs
fresh cuts sold to retailers and processors
raising hogs for its own plants
moat: Scale and vertical integration from the hog farm to the packaged bacon, which spreads costs across the chain and makes it the low-cost supplier of American pork.
risks: Hog prices and feed costs swing the results hard
Export demand depends on Chinese and Mexican trade policy
Chinese ownership through WH Group draws political attention in the United States
opportunities: 8.3 times earnings and 8.0 times free cash flow with $927M of free cash flow
The packaged meats half earns steady branded margins regardless of the hog cycle
Analysts see about 21% upside, with $1.5B of cash against $2.4B of debt
watch: Packaged meats margins and hog production profitability.
